items.title: Operationalizing CHAI: Translating Coalition for Health AI Governance Playbooks into Oracle Cloud ERP Controls
items.abstract: Healthcare organizations are enabling AI-embedded ERP features faster than governance rules are being written for them, and in mid-2026 the rules arrived faster than most solution architects expected. The Coalition for Health AI published eight governance playbooks on 27 May 2026, and five days later the Joint Commission opened its voluntary Responsible Use of AI in Healthcare certification, which means a surveyor can now ask a health system to demonstrate its AI governance rather than describe it. Neither document specifies which system setting enforces any of it, and arguably neither should, since both are written to apply across every vendor a health system might run. This paper closes that gap for one platform. Six governance domains running through the CHAI playbooks and RUAIH guidance, namely accountability, transparency, human oversight, pre-deployment risk assessment, continuous monitoring, and third-party risk, are each mapped to a control that already exists inside Oracle Cloud ERP: role-based security profiles, approval hierarchies, and the execution traceability introduced with Oracle's 2026 Fusion Agentic Applications and AI Agent Studio. The mapping is supported by a four-tier risk model that determines how much autonomy an agent may hold, an audit evidence model stating what a surveyor should be shown for each domain, and a six-step implementation sequence. The contribution is a practitioner synthesis drawn from Oracle Cloud ERP transformation programs in regulated health systems. It is not a controlled study, and no compliance outcome, audit finding rate, or certification result is reported or claimed.

items.title: Opinion Mining for Product Reviews Using Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: The rapid growth of e-commerce platforms has resulted in a large volume of customer-generated product reviews. These reviews contain valuable information about customer opinions, satisfaction levels, product quality, and specific product features. However, manually analysing a large number of reviews is time-consuming and difficult. Opinion mining, also known as sentiment analysis, uses Artificial Intelligence and Natural Language Processing techniques to automatically identify and classify opinions expressed in textual reviews. This paper presents a conceptual AI-based framework for analysing product reviews and identifying their sentiment polarity as positive, negative, or neutral. The proposed approach combines contextual language representation using Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) with aspect-based sentiment analysis inspired by Aspect-specific Graph Convolutional Networks (ASGCN). The system performs review preprocessing, contextual feature extraction, aspect identification, sentiment classification, and generation of an overall opinion summary. The reviewed literature also includes hybrid BERT-CNN architectures, user/context-aware graph modelling, and multimodal learning approaches, which provide additional directions for improving opinion analysis. The proposed framework aims to provide more detailed and meaningful information than simple positive or negative classification by identifying the product aspects responsible for customer opinions. Such a system can assist customers in decision-making and help businesses understand product strengths, weaknesses, and areas requiring improvement

items.title: Opportunities and risks of AI in lesson planning: insights from pre-service teachers
items.abstract: This contribution presents an exploratory study on pre-service teachers' perceptions of the use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in lesson planning, with a focus on opportunities, risks, and conditions for effective integration into instructional design. The study is grounded in the TPACK framework (Mishra & Koehler, 2006) and its extension Intelligent-TPACK (Celik, 2023), which incorporates an explicit ethical dimension into teachers' technological and pedagogical knowledge. Within this perspective, AI tools such as chatbots, intelligent tutoring systems, and automated planning systems are not neutral instruments but sociotechnical systems that require critical evaluation in terms of transparency, fairness, and accountability. The theoretical approach adopted here is further informed by critical AI literacy perspectives, which emphasise the need for teachers to develop not only operational competence but also the ability to interrogate the assumptions and biases embedded in algorithmic outputs. items.title: Optimalisasi Bimbingan Belajar Bahasa Arab Berbasis Nilai-Nilai Akhlak sebagai Upaya Pencegahan Putus Sekolah di Daerah Terpencil
items.abstract: This study aims to examine the effectiveness of the Arabic language tutoring program (bimbingan belajar Bahasa Arab) at SMK Negeri 1 Mesuji, Ogan Komering Ilir Regency, where the dropout rate reaches 17.3%, and to formulate an optimization model for that program grounded in Pendidikan Akidah Akhlak (Islamic Creed and Morals Education) to build students' character and resilience and to prevent dropout. This explanatory sequential mixed-methods study used primary data from students, teachers, and parents. Of the students actively participating in the Arabic language tutoring program, 50 respondents were selected through stratified random sampling (Slovin formula) to complete a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire, which was analyzed using multiple linear regression in SPSS 26. Qualitative data were collected through in-depth interviews, focus group discussions, and participant observation with key informants selected through purposive sampling, and were analyzed thematically using NVivo 12. Quantitative results show that the effectiveness of the Arabic language tutoring was mostly in the moderate category (76%) and did not significantly affect Akidah Akhlak-based resilience (t = 0.340; sig = 0.735), whereas intrinsic motivation did (t = 2.587; sig = 0.013; R² = 0.400). Qualitative findings show that informants regard the Arabic tutoring as helpful for understanding the material yet still academically oriented, that spiritual resilience is students' primary coping mechanism against external constraints, and that all informants expect an Arabic language tutoring model that integrates Akidah Akhlak. The study proposes an optimization model for Arabic language tutoring built on five strategies: integrating Akidah Akhlak values into Arabic tutoring materials, strengthening intrinsic motivation and character, adopting a holistic learning approach, fostering school–teacher–parent collaboration, and providing continuous mentoring for students at risk of dropping out.

items.title: Orchestrating Big Data and Artificial Intelligence for Adaptive Digital Business Strategy
items.abstract: The rapid acceleration of digital transformation has changed the way organizations formulate and implement business strategies, requiring firms to become more adaptive, data-driven, and responsive to dynamic market conditions. This study aims to examine how big data and artificial intelligence can be orchestrated as integrated strategic capabilities to support adaptive digital business strategy. Using a qualitative conceptual approach, this study applies a structured literature review and thematic synthesis to analyze previous studies related to big data capability, artificial intelligence capability, governance mechanisms, intelligent business insight, and strategic adaptability. The results show that big data functions as a strategic foundation by providing diverse information from customers, markets, operations, and digital platforms, while artificial intelligence acts as an intelligent decision engine that transforms data into predictions, recommendations, automation, and actionable business insights. The findings also indicate that governance and human decision-making are essential in ensuring that the use of big data and AI remains reliable, transparent, accountable, secure, and aligned with organizational objectives. This study concludes that adaptive digital business strategy emerges from the continuous orchestration of data resources, AI systems, governance structures, human judgment, and strategic execution. The proposed framework contributes to digital business literature by explaining how AI-driven big data orchestration can improve decision quality, agility, competitiveness, innovation, operational efficiency, and sustainable digital value creation. In addition, the discussion is expanded to include cybersecurity, data privacy, secure data processing, and AI risk management as critical enablers of large-scale data-driven business systems.

items.title: Organisational Development and Industrial Democracy
items.abstract: This chapter provides an overview of Eric Miller’s contribution to organizational development and industrial democracy, situating his practice within the Tavistock tradition that integrates open systems thinking, socio-technical systems (STS) design, and psychoanalytic perspectives on group and organizational life. Miller argued that organizations are not merely rational structures, but emotional and social systems in which anxiety, defence, and unconscious processes shape behaviour, decision-making, and capacity for change. Central to his approach is the concept of the organization as an open system whose viability depends on effective boundary management, between sub-systems, levels of authority, and the organization and its environment. Building on STS principles, Miller emphasized joint optimization: designing technical processes and social arrangements in tandem so that task requirements and human needs are aligned. He extended this work by making visible the defensive patterns that emerge under stress, splitting, projection, denial, scapegoating, and rigidity, and by showing how authority and leadership often become focal points for organizational anxieties. His consultancy therefore combined structural diagnosis with reflective inquiry into role, power, and emotional experience. The chapter illustrates these themes through emblematic cases: the coal mining studies that shaped STS foundations; applications in healthcare where hierarchy and communication can become defensive; work with the Church of England on identity and authority in a changing environment; and the Norwegian Industrial Democracy Project, demonstrating how participative work design can enhance resilience and performance. Overall, this part frames Miller’s legacy as a disciplined, practice-oriented synthesis of system and psyche, offering enduring concepts for contemporary organizational change.

items.title: Organizational mechanisms in digital public health transformation: change communication, collective sensemaking, and cross-functional collaboration
items.abstract: Introduction Digital public health transformation extends beyond technology deployment and requires organizational processes that align interpretation, coordination, governance, and population-health goals. Existing research examines change communication, collective sensemaking, and cross-functional collaboration separately, with limited integration of their boundaries, recursive interactions, cross-level transmission, and multilevel outcomes. This review develops an organizational explanation of how these mechanisms may support transformation. Methods A narrative integrative review synthesized theoretical, empirical, policy, and technical literature from organizational science, implementation science, digital public health, data governance, and artificial intelligence governance. Searches covered PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, APA PsycINFO, CINAHL, IEEE Xplore, ProQuest Public Health Database, Business Source Complete, and traceable institutional sources from inception to October 1, 2026. Sources were purposively selected for relevance, contribution, public health applicability, analytical level, and traceability. Synthesis used construct coding, within-theme comparison, framework comparison, cross-level mechanism mapping, and analysis of competing explanations and evidence boundaries. Results Change communication establishes credible and contestable direction; collective sensemaking develops shared problem representations; cross-functional collaboration translates shared understanding into coordinated action. They operate recursively rather than sequentially. A seven-layer framework links structural contextual conditions, organizational mechanisms, potential mediating capabilities, implementation outcomes, organizational or system outcomes, population-level service and equity outcomes, and population health outcomes. Team psychological safety moderates the relationship between proximal support conditions and risk-detection behaviors, which feed back into the mechanisms. Organizational readiness for change, knowledge absorption and translation, interoperability governance, organizational learning, and resilience are proposed as mediating capabilities. Power and equity governance, community decision rights, representativeness, vendor accountability, auditing, appeals, portability, and exit management cut across the framework. The model complements CFIR, NASSS, i-PARIHS, EPIS, and sociotechnical approaches by specifying observable interactive mechanisms and feedback pathways. Discussion The framework provides a testable explanatory structure and governance-diagnostic tool for surveillance, data infrastructures, laboratory networks, artificial intelligence, and community co-production. Evidence more strongly supports organizational and system processes than causal effects on population health. Longitudinal, multilevel, and mechanism-oriented studies should test mediation, moderation, feedback, equity, and cross-level transmission.

items.title: Overtrust in Generative AI and Students’ Critical Thinking: An Integrated PLS-SEM and Machine Learning Analysis in Vietnamese Higher Education
items.abstract: The rapid adoption of generative AI (GenAI) among university students has raised concerns that excessive trust in AI outputs may erode critical thinking. This study examines how overtrust relates to critical thinking through cognitive offloading and AI dependency, with AI literacy as a protective moderator, integrating partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) with machine learning. Survey data from 580 Vietnamese undergraduates were analysed through a five-step pipeline: exploratory structure learning, confirmatory path estimation, predictive benchmarking, explainable AI, and heterogeneous-effect estimation. Overtrust was associated with higher offloading (β = 0.390) and dependency (β = 0.402), both of which were associated with lower critical thinking (β = -0.251 and -0.348), while AI literacy buffered the association with dependency (interaction β = 0.154). Crucially, the direct effect of overtrust was non-significant and the two mediators carried 89% of its total effect, indicating indirect-only mediation. A parsimonious six-variable classifier separated at-risk students with AUC ≈ 0.77, whereas demographics alone performed at chance; SHAP analysis identified AI dependency as the dominant feature in the classification decision, and a causal forest confirmed the buffering pattern across the low-to-mid range while exposing a non-monotonic reversal under sparse support at the upper tail. Interventions should therefore target AI-use behaviour rather than trust itself. These findings are associational rather than causal: the design is cross-sectional with all measures self-reported at a single point, so the classifier performs concurrent screening rather than temporal prediction.

items.title: Pedagogy and teaching in emergency contexts in the age Of artificial intelligence: towards a human-centred Framework for educational continuity, inclusion and Resilience
items.abstract: The contemporary global educational landscape is increasingly vulnerable to systemic crises, including natural disasters, public health emergencies, armed conflicts, and socioeconomic instability. These events do not merely interrupt educational continuity; they exacerbate existing social, economic, and geographic inequalities, disproportionately affecting vulnerable populations (Burde et al., 2017). In this context, Education in Emergencies (EiE) must be understood not only as a temporary humanitarian response, but as a structural and pedagogical imperative for safeguarding the universal right to education. Educational resilience therefore requires a shift from reactive and fragmented models toward proactive and adaptive systems capable of anticipating, absorbing, and recovering from crises without compromising the quality and equity of teaching and learning. This resilience cannot be achieved without integrating the psychological, emotional, and relational dimensions of education. Trauma-informed education highlights how large-scale crises can profoundly affect students, families, and teachers, altering stress regulation and compromising cognitive, executive, and socio-relational functioning essential to learning (Avery et al., 2021; Berger, 2024). Chapter in: Francesco Peluso Cassese (ed.), Algorithmic Heartbeats: Affective Education in the Age of the Fourth Revolution, REN Press – Cares srl, 2026, pp. 205-207. ISBN 979-12-82860-00-0. Volume DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23211262. Section: Hybrid and "Emotionally Aware" Learning Environments.

items.title: Pelvic floor ultrasound in functional assessment and rehabilitation: current applications and standardization challenges
items.abstract: Introduction: Pelvic floor ultrasound has evolved over the past 2 decades from a predominantly anatomical imaging modality into a tool supporting functional assessment and rehabilitation. Its capability of visualizing pelvic floor structures in real time during contraction, relaxation, coughing, and straining has expanded its role beyond structural diagnosis and into physiotherapy practice. Aim: This narrative review aimed to examine the role of pelvic floor ultrasound in functional assessment and rehabilitation, with particular emphasis on ultrasound‑derived functional parameters and challenges related to standardization. Methods: Relevant literature was identified through searches of the PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases, focusing on pelvic floor muscle function, rehabilitative ultrasound imaging, biofeedback, physiotherapy applications, and emerging ultrasound technologies. Results: Current evidence supports the transition of ultrasound from static anatomical imaging toward dynamic assessment of pelvic floor muscle performance. Commonly reported functional parameters include bladder neck mobility, pelvic floor elevation, levator hiatus dimensions, and hiatal reduction during contraction. Among these, levator hiatus dynamics appear to provide particularly meaningful information on the integrated mechanical effect of levator ani activation. Ultrasound may also support biofeedback, motor learning, individualized exercise instruction, and monitoring of treatment‑related changes. Emerging approaches, including shear‑wave elastography, automated image analysis, and artificial intelligence–assisted assessment, can make measurements less dependent on manual interpretation. Conclusions: Despite recent advances, functional pelvic floor ultrasound remains limited by heterogeneity in acquisition protocols, task instructions, outcome measures, and reporting methods. Future research should focus on consensus‑based protocols, core functional outcomes, structured reporting, and clinically meaningful reference values.

items.title: PENGGUNAAN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE DALAM PENILAIAN RISIKO NASABAH PEMBIAYAAN SYARIAH
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in customer risk assessment offers Islamic financial institutions opportunities to process information more systematically, while also raising legal concerns regarding the limits of technological authority and legal accountability for financing decisions. This study aims to examine the position of AI in customer risk assessment and the legal responsibilities of Islamic financial institutions in its application. The study employs normative legal research using statutory and conceptual approaches. The analysis involves examining legal provisions concerning Islamic banking, personal data protection, customer protection, and technology governance, followed by an assessment of these provisions in relation to the principles of prudence and accountability in AI utilization. The findings indicate that AI can support data processing, identify risk patterns, and provide information to inform the assessment of prospective customers’ financing eligibility. However, algorithmic outputs cannot replace the professional judgment and legal responsibility of the institution authorized to make financing decisions. Islamic financial institutions remain obligated to supervise analytical outputs, ensure that data are used in accordance with applicable regulations, and maintain fairness, information security, and compliance with Sharia principles. This study concludes that AI implementation must be supported by adequate governance and meaningful human oversight to ensure that technological efficiency remains balanced with customer legal protection and accountability for financing decisions. ABSTRAK Pemanfaatan Artificial Intelligence (AI) dalam penilaian risiko nasabah membuka peluang bagi lembaga keuangan syariah untuk mengolah informasi secara lebih sistematis, tetapi sekaligus menimbulkan persoalan mengenai batas kewenangan teknologi dan pertanggungjawaban hukum atas keputusan pembiayaan. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis kedudukan AI dalam proses penilaian risiko nasabah serta tanggung jawab lembaga keuangan syariah atas penggunaannya. Penelitian menggunakan metode hukum normatif dengan pendekatan perundang-undangan dan konseptual. Analisis dilakukan melalui penelaahan ketentuan hukum yang berkaitan dengan perbankan syariah, pelindungan data pribadi, perlindungan nasabah, dan tata kelola teknologi, kemudian dikaitkan dengan konsep kehati-hatian serta akuntabilitas dalam penggunaan AI. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa AI dapat dimanfaatkan untuk membantu pemrosesan data, mengenali pola risiko, dan menyediakan informasi sebagai bahan pertimbangan dalam menilai kelayakan calon nasabah. Namun, keluaran algoritma tidak dapat diperlakukan sebagai pengganti penilaian dan tanggung jawab hukum lembaga yang berwenang mengambil keputusan pembiayaan. Lembaga keuangan syariah tetap berkewajiban mengawasi hasil analisis, memastikan penggunaan data sesuai ketentuan, serta menjaga keadilan, keamanan informasi, dan kepatuhan terhadap prinsip syariah. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa penerapan AI perlu disertai tata kelola yang memadai dan pengawasan manusia agar efisiensi teknologi berjalan seimbang dengan perlindungan hukum nasabah dan akuntabilitas keputusan pembiayaan.

items.title: Perception and Challenges of Using Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Post Graduate Medical Education in Dar Es Salaam, Tanzania
items.abstract: Abstract Background Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being integrated into healthcare and medical education, offering opportunities to enhance learning, teaching, and clinical decision-making. While AI has demonstrated considerable potential in medical training, evidence regarding its use in postgraduate medical education in low- and middle-income countries remains limited. This study explored the perceptions and challenges associated with AI use among postgraduate medical residents and faculty members in Tanzania and identified educational needs for its effective integration into training programs. Methods A descriptive qualitative study was conducted among postgraduate medical residents and faculty members from three universities offering postgraduate medical education in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. Participants were purposively selected to ensure representation across specialties and levels of training. Data were collected through four focus group discussions with residents and thirteen key informant interviews with faculty members. Audio-recorded interviews were transcribed verbatim and analysed using conventional content analysis with the aid of MAXQDA version 24. The study was reported in accordance with the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ) guidelines. Results A total of 40 participants (27 residents and 13 faculty members) were included. Five major themes emerged from the analysis: (1) AI as a supportive learning tool that enhances understanding and educational efficiency; (2) concerns that excessive reliance on AI may undermine clinical reasoning and academic integrity; (3) limitations in the accuracy, reliability, and contextual relevance of AI-generated information; (4) barriers to effective AI use within the local context; and (5) the need for structured institutional support to guide safe and effective AI use. Participants reported that AI improved learning efficiency, facilitated access to information, simplified complex concepts, and enhanced teaching productivity. However, concerns were raised regarding overdependence on AI, reduced critical thinking, fabricated references, inconsistent outputs, and limited applicability of AI-generated recommendations to the Tanzanian healthcare context. Financial constraints, limited local data, and lack of formal AI training were identified as important barriers to effective AI utilization. Conclusions AI is perceived as a valuable adjunct to postgraduate medical education in Tanzania, with the potential to enhance learning and teaching practices. However, concerns regarding overreliance, information reliability, contextual applicability, and inadequate institutional guidance remain significant barriers to its effective use. Structured training, institutional policies, and equitable access to reliable AI platforms are essential to support the responsible integration of AI into postgraduate medical education.

items.title: Perception of AI-Generated Versus Human-Made Images: A Cross-Sectional Comparative Study (2023 vs. 2026)
items.abstract: With the rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence, distinguishing AI-generated images from human-created ones has become increasingly difficult. This paper presents a cross-sectional comparative study examining people’s ability to differentiate between AI-generated and human-made visual content in 2023 (N = 51) and 2026 (N = 154). Using a highly consistent experimental design, participants rated 36 images (18 AI-generated and 18 human-made) on a 7-point Likert scale (1 = definitely human-made to 7 = definitely AI-generated) across three categories: portraits, nature, and graphic logos. The same human-made images were used in both studies, while the AI images in 2026 were generated exclusively with Midjourney. Results showed that participants could still significantly distinguish AI-generated from human-made images in both years. However, the magnitude of differentiation decreased noticeably from 2023 to 2026. The largest and most consistent difference was observed in the portrait category (2023: Z = −6.093, p < 0.001; 2026: Z = −9.343, p < 0.001). Significant differences were also found in the logo category in both years (2023: Z = −5.381, p < 0.001; 2026: Z = −5.177, p < 0.001). In 2023, human-made logos were rated as more human-like than AI-generated logos. In 2026, the direction reversed: human-made logos were rated as more AI-like than Midjourney logos. Nature images were the most difficult to classify overall. While a significant difference existed in 2023 (Z = −5.773, p < 0.001), this difference disappeared in 2026 (Z = 1.671, p = 0.095). When asked which images were the most difficult to evaluate in 2026, participants identified logos as the most challenging (51.6%), followed by nature scenes (34.8%) and portraits (13.5%). These findings indicate that participants could still distinguish AI-generated from human-made images, but the contrast was smaller in 2026 than in 2023. This change cannot be attributed to human ability alone, because the AI stimuli and the samples also differed between waves and thus cannot be directly compared. The study highlights growing challenges regarding visual authenticity in the digital age and discusses implications for media literacy and public trust.

items.title: Performance of artificial intelligence-assisted cytology and high-risk human papillomavirus testing for cervical cancer screening
items.abstract: Evidence comparing cervical cancer screening strategies that combine artificial intelligence-assisted liquid-based cytology (AI-LBC) and high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) testing in large-scale populations is limited. This study includes 284,002 women who underwent AI-LBC and HR-HPV genotyping in community-based screening in Wuhan, China. We evaluate the performance of nine hypothesized screening strategies in detecting cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse (CIN2+) and their colposcopy referral rates. After correcting for verification bias, HR-HPV testing alone (Strategy 4) demonstrates higher sensitivity (94.93% vs. 83.88%) and a higher Youden’s index (0.864 vs. 0.789) than AI-LBC alone (Strategy 1), but requires a higher referral rate (9.05% vs. 5.49%). Among the triage-based strategies, Strategy 3 (AI-LBC with reflex HR-HPV) achieves a sensitivity of 82.90%, a referral rate of 2.67%, and a Youden’s index of 0.807. HR-HPV genotyping with reflex AI-LBC (Strategy 7) demonstrates a sensitivity of 92.68%, a Youden’s index of 0.899, and a referral rate of 3.34%. Co-testing of AI-LBC and HR-HPV genotyping (Strategy 9) achieves the highest Youden’s index (0.932), with a sensitivity of 96.37% and a referral rate of 3.70%. These findings suggest that AI-LBC performs well as a standalone screening method, triage tool, or a component a co-testing strategy in cervical cancer screening. When HR-HPV genotyping is available, Strategy 7 or Strategy 9 may be considered, depending on the trade-off between detection performance and referral burden. The authors prove AI-assisted cytology effective for cervical cancer screening. When combined with HPV testing, it detects more precancerous lesions and maintains low referral rates.

items.title: Performing with the Forest and to the Forest
items.abstract: Abstract This chapter explores Anna Fiere’s Tree Opera, a contemporary site-specific project commissioned by the Mustarinda Association and based on Finnish- Latvian collaboration, as an example of interspecies performance that aspires to a non-anthropocentric way of making (Western) opera. We analyse the co-constitutive relations of the opera’s staging, libretto, and musical, vocal expression with the old-growth forests in Hyrynsalmi, Finland, next to which the project had its first performances. The grounding of Tree Opera in such relations results in what we call a more-than-human performance collective, which highlights the fundamental, albeit contextually specific, dependence of human existence, including artistic practices, on the thriving of other species and nature. Our main argument is that this opera performance project engages in aesthetic activism as an example of ecocritical art. This means that it encourages awareness of the vital importance of natural ecosystems in the age of the ecological crisis through its sensorial and performative characteristics and the audience perceptions these enable, instead of incorporating explicit political messaging.

items.title: Personalized Use of ChatGPT and Its Association with Autonomous Learning among University Students
items.abstract: This study examined the association between personalized use of ChatGPT and autonomous learning among university students. A quantitative, non-experimental, cross-sectional, correlational study was conducted with 500 students from an Ecuadorian higher education institution. Two questionnaires were administered to assess the perceived personalization of ChatGPT use and autonomous learning. The results showed a positive and statistically significant association between the two variables (ρ = 0,61; p < 0,001). Likewise, content personalization (ρ = 0,54), learning-process personalization (ρ = 0,46), and interaction personalization (ρ = 0,49) showed moderate associations with autonomous learning. The findings indicate that higher perceived levels of personalization tend to coexist with higher levels of academic autonomy; however, the study design does not permit causal inferences.

items.title: Physiology-informed deep learning for early identification of sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy from echocardiographic cine loops: a multicenter development and external validation study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy (SICM) is heterogeneous and may involve abnormalities in cardiac contraction, relaxation, and beat-to-beat motion. Conventional echocardiographic measurements and cardiac troponin T (cTnT) may not fully capture dynamic changes in myocardial function during sepsis. We developed a physiology-informed deep-learning framework for early identification of SICM from apical four-chamber (A4C) echocardiographic cine loops. Methods Adult patients with sepsis were retrospectively identified from two centers. The first eligible A4C cine loop obtained within 24 h after sepsis onset was used for model development. SICM was defined by cardiac abnormalities observed during the septic episode. Cine loops were divided into physiologically aligned end-diastole-to-end-diastole cardiac cycles. The model combined EchoJEPA-based visual representation learning with phase-aware spatial and temporal modeling, LV area-derived physiological features, and multi-cycle aggregation. Internal validation was performed using patient-level grouped fivefold cross-validation. The final model was trained in the full development cohort and independently evaluated in MIMIC-IV-ECHO using a conventional cTnT-based SICM phenotype. Model performance was compared with direct EchoJEPA classification. Results The development cohort included 530 patients, including 305 with SICM and 225 sepsis-only controls. In patient-level grouped fivefold cross-validation, the physiology-informed model achieved an out-of-fold AUROC of 0.933 (95% CI, 0.910–0.954). The external cohort included 93 patients, including 39 with SICM and 54 sepsis-only controls. The model achieved an AUROC of 0.929 (95% CI, 0.864–0.980). The direct EchoJEPA baseline achieved an external AUROC of 0.735 (95% CI, 0.632–0.833). The paired difference in AUROC was 0.194 (95% CI, 0.095–0.294; DeLong test, P < 0.001). Results remained consistent in sensitivity analyses using alternative cTnT definitions. Conclusions A physiology-informed deep-learning framework enabled early identification of SICM from routinely acquired A4C cine loops and maintained discrimination in both internal cross-validation and an independent external cohort. Incorporating cardiac physiology into EchoJEPA improved discrimination compared with direct foundation-model classification. These findings support further prospective evaluation of physiology-informed echocardiographic video analysis for early identification of SICM.

items.title: Polyphonic Creativity
items.abstract: Abstract As generative AI (GenAI) continues to reshape educational landscapes, its impact on creativity in learning demands critical examination. This chapter examines key opportunities and challenges of using GenAI to foster creativity in education, particularly AI’s role in reshaping creative processes within schools and higher education, emphasizing how GenAI functions as both a co-creator and collaborator in the learning process. Building on existing theoretical frameworks, this chapter integrates current research on hybrid human–AI collaboration, particularly through the notion of polyphonic creativity, which expands on Bakhtin’s notion of polyphony. This framework highlights how multiple voices—both human and AI—interact in dynamic tension to drive creative knowledge processes. The chapter further extends this perspective by applying the STEPRE model, demonstrating how structured learning environments can scaffold AI-enhanced creativity while preserving dialogic engagement. The integration of AI in education is not without challenges. A key concern is ensuring that AI enhances rather than undermines independent creative thought. This chapter underscores the importance of AI literacy among educators and ethical awareness in AI integration to harness AI’s creative potential responsibly. As AI technology continues to evolve, its role in education will likely expand, necessitating thoughtful, research-informed approaches to co-creativity that preserve human agency while leveraging the computational power of AI. Although grounded in Nordic contexts, the models and practices described are applicable across diverse international education systems.

items.title: POSITIVE AND NEGATIVE IMPACTS OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON THE ACTIVITIES OF STUDENT YOUTH: A SYSTEMATIC-ANALYTICAL APPROACH
items.abstract: The article analyzes the positive and negative effects of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly generative language models, on the academic, research, cognitive and social activities of university students. Following the IMRAD structure, a systematic-analytical review was conducted in line with the transparency principles of PRISMA 2020. The findings reveal AI's potential to enhance learning performance, personalization, academic writing and research productivity, alongside the risks of excessive cognitive offloading, weakened critical thinking, threats to academic integrity, model hallucinations and digital inequality. The direction of impact is determined not by AI itself but by the mode of use (scaffolding versus substitution). A four-level framework of recommendations for the responsible use of AI in higher education institutions is proposed.

items.title: PoSSUM: a protocol for surveying social-media users with multimodal LLMs
items.abstract: This paper introduces PoSSUM , an open-source protocol for unobtrusive polling of social media users via multimodal Large Language Models (LLMs). PoSSUM leverages users’ real-time posts, images, and other digital traces to create silicon samples that capture information not present in the LLM’s training data. To obtain representative estimates, PoSSUM employs Multilevel Regression and Post-stratification (MrP) with structured priors to counteract the observable selection biases of social media platforms. The protocol’s aggregate predictive performance is evaluated during the 2024 US Presidential Election, for which five PoSSUM polls were conducted and published on GitHub and \(\mathbb{X}\) . In the final poll, fielded October 17–26 with a synthetic sample of 1054 \(\mathbb{X}\) users, PoSSUM accurately predicted the outcomes in 50 of 51 states and assigned the Republican candidate a win probability of 0.65. Notably, it also exhibited lower state-level bias than most established pollsters. These results point to PoSSUM ’s potential as a fully automated, unobtrusive alternative to traditional survey methods, whilst highlighting the need for further validation across contexts and outcomes.

items.title: Pre-service teachers' perceptions of Artificial Intelligence: an exploratory study on current uses and professional projections
items.abstract: The growing integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into university contexts is today a relevant theme for contemporary pedagogy (Floridi, 2022; Rivoltella, 2020), in a context in which the introduction of AI questions the very nature of the educational experience (Carlomagno, Vadalà & Ricciardi, 2026). The condition of students of Scienze della Formazione Primaria (Primary Teacher Education) takes on relevance here, since they encounter AI in their study path and, as future teachers, envisage its use in their future teaching practice. This exploratory study investigates its current uses, professional projections and the students' emotional experiences, with specific attention to the anxiety expressed towards such technologies. The analysis adopts two reference constructs, AI literacy (Ng et al., 2021) and AI anxiety (Wang & Wang, 2019), read within an enactivist-interactionist frame that conceives knowledge not as a transfer of content, but as a process emerging from the situated and embodied interaction between subject and environment (Varela, Thompson & Rosch, 1991). items.title: Precision Nanomedicine for Glioblastoma: Engineering Nanoparticles to Overcome the Blood–Brain Barrier, Tumour Heterogeneity and Therapeutic Resistance
items.abstract: Glioblastoma GBM) is the most aggressive primary malignant brain tumor, with poor clinical outcomes despite maximal surgical resection, radiotherapy, and temozolomide chemotherapy. The limited effectiveness of current therapies is largely associated with the restrictive blood–brain barrier (BBB) and blood–tumor barrier (BTB), extensive intratumoral heterogeneity, glioma stem cell populations, and multiple mechanisms of therapeutic resistance. Nanomedicine offers a promising strategy to address these interconnected challenges through rationally engineered nanoparticles capable of improving brain delivery and therapeutic specificity. This review discusses current approaches for overcoming the BBB/BTB, including receptor-mediated transcytosis, focused ultrasound, convection-enhanced delivery, and intranasal administration. Major nanocarrier platforms, including liposomes, solid lipid nanoparticles, polymeric nanoparticles, dendrimers, metallic nanoparticles, mesoporous silica nanoparticles, and extracellular vesicles, are examined for their therapeutic and theranostic potential. Particular emphasis is placed on multifunctional systems designed to target molecularly heterogeneous GBM populations and overcome resistance mechanisms involving MGMT-mediated DNA repair, drug efflux, PI3K/AKT signaling, and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments. Emerging strategies integrating biomarker-guided targeting, co-delivery systems, theranostics, artificial intelligence, machine learning, patient-derived organoids, and humanized BBB models may enable personalized nanomedicine. However, challenges involving biological translation, protein corona formation, manufacturing, regulatory requirements, and clinical accessibility remain. Integrated and patient-specific nanoparticle design may provide a future pathway toward more effective precision treatment of GBM.

items.title: Predicting the Risk of MSME Bankruptcy in Kupang City: Integrating the Altman Z-Score, Macroeconomic Impact, Machine Learning, and Explainable AI (SHAP and LIME)
items.abstract: This study aims to assess the financial health and predict the bankruptcy risk of 100 micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Kupang City by integrating the Altman Z′′ score, testing the impact of macroeconomic variables, machine learning modeling , and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). Data completeness was tested with Little's MCAR test, the impact of macroeconomics (inflation, deposit interest rates, and rupiah exchange rates) on the Z′′ score was tested with the Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test, and four classification algorithms (Gradient Boosting, Random Forest, Logistic Regression, and Naive Bayes) were compared on 11 selected features, then the best model was explained with SHAP and LIME. The results showed that missing data was perfectly random (Sig. 0.587) and all MSMEs experienced a decrease in health scores after macroeconomic factors were included (Z = −8.697; Sig. 0.000). Gradient Boosting provides the best performance in accuracy, precision, recall , and F1-score (80%; 0.83; 0.71; 0.77) with an AUC of 0.85. SHAP analysis places D2, total current assets, and D1 indicators as global determinants, while LIME on three MSMEs shows that low D2 and limited total current assets drive the prediction of bankruptcy risk in MSME #2. These findings confirm that assessments based on internal data alone tend to be overly optimistic and that the combination of predictive models with transparent explanations can be the basis of an early warning system for businesses, banks, and local governments.

items.abstract: This study examined the potential interaction between automation reliability and automation transparency in the context of a weather-related decision to close a school in the face of a forecast blizzard. Participants received snowfall and closure advice from four different weather services dependent upon an automation weather model that differed in its degree of reliability (100% vs. 67%). Two of the services simply provided advice, and for two of them, this advice was accompanied by transparency in the form of the raw data, or weather symptoms display that was input into the weather model. The results revealed that degraded reliability of the automation lowered trust in and dependence on the advice and hurt overall accuracy. In a significant interaction, these degraded effects were mitigated by automation transparency. These findings were interpreted in terms of a mechanism of optimal attention allocated (weighting) between the raw data transparency and the weather service advice.

items.title: Prediksi Performa Akademik Siswa Menggunakan Machine Learning Berbasis Feature Engineering dan Explainable AI: Predicting Student Academic Performance Using Machine Learning with Feature Engineering and Explainable AI
items.abstract: Perkembangan machine learning dalam bidang pendidikan memungkinkan pemanfaatan data untuk memprediksi performa akademik siswa sehingga dapat mendukung deteksi dini dan perumusan intervensi yang lebih tepat. Namun, sebagian penelitian masih berfokus pada peningkatan akurasi, sementara pengembangan representasi fitur berbasis pengetahuan domain (domain knowledge) untuk menggambarkan faktor sosioekonomi dan dukungan orang tua masih terbatas. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk membangun model prediksi yang tidak hanya akurat tetapi juga mudah diinterpretasikan melalui integrasi feature engineering dan pendekatan Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI). Dataset yang digunakan terdiri dari 6.607 data siswa dengan 20 fitur. Tiga fitur baru dikembangkan, yaitu Study_Efficiency, Socioeconomic_Index, dan Parental_Support_Index. Selanjutnya, tujuh algoritma regresi dioptimasi menggunakan hyperparameter tuning dan dievaluasi berdasarkan Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), , serta 10-fold cross-validation. Hasil menunjukkan bahwa model Lasso memberikan performa terbaik dengan sebesar 0,7710 pada data uji dan 0,7392 0,1089 pada cross-validation. Analisis SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) dan Partial Dependence Plot (PDP) menunjukkan bahwa faktor perilaku seperti Attendance dan Hours_Studied memiliki kontribusi yang lebih dominan, sementara fitur hasil rekayasa membantu merepresentasikan faktor sosioekonomi secara lebih terstruktur. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa model linear dengan representasi fitur yang sesuai dapat memberikan performa yang kompetitif sekaligus tetap transparan.

items.title: Preparing Future Generations Amid the Development of Artificial Intelligence: A Literature Review of Digital Literacy, Ethics, and Self-Directed Learning among Elementary School Students
items.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming elementary education, creating opportunities for personalized learning while raising concerns about information reliability, ethical responsibility, and student autonomy. This study aimed to synthesize how digital literacy, ethical awareness, and self-directed learning can contribute to preparing elementary school students for AI-integrated education. An integrative literature review was conducted using relevant scholarly publications, primarily published between 2021 and 2026. The literature was examined through qualitative content analysis and thematic synthesis to identify key concepts, recurring findings, educational challenges, and relationships among the three dimensions. The findings indicate that digital literacy requires students to critically evaluate AI-generated information, verify claims, and recognize the limitations of automated systems. Ethical awareness encompasses responsible technology use, privacy protection, fairness, academic integrity, and informed decision-making. Meanwhile, self-directed learning involves setting learning goals, selecting appropriate resources, monitoring understanding, and reflecting on learning outcomes. Although AI can facilitate exploration, feedback, and personalized learning, its educational benefits are not guaranteed and depend on instructional design, teacher guidance, and students’ active engagement. This study proposes an integrated conceptual framework in which digital literacy, ethical awareness, and self-directed learning function as mutually reinforcing dimensions of AI readiness, supported by teachers, schools, and families. The review concludes that preparing elementary school students for an AI-mediated future requires an educational approach that combines critical judgment, ethical responsibility, and learner agency. Further empirical research is needed to validate the framework and examine its applicability across diverse educational contexts.

items.abstract: The article addresses the problem of the formation of engineering thinking in senior secondary school students under the conditions of widespread use of generative artificial intelligence. It is shown that turning to a large language model when solving an engineering task shifts the student from the position of a subject of inquiry to that of a recipient of a ready-made answer. Drawing on the culturological and subject-activity approaches, the author justifies the preservation of the senior student's position as a subject in interaction with generative AI as a self-standing didactic condition for the formation of engineering thinking.

items.title: Prevalence, knowledge and predictors of Text Neck Syndrome among undergraduate students in East Khasi Hills, Meghalaya, India: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Background: Young adults' extensive use of smartphones has resulted in several health concerns and one of which is Text Neck Syndrome. Prolonged neck flexion during smartphone use can lead to neck pain, disability and functional limitations. The study focused on determining the prevalence and knowledge regarding Text Neck Syndrome and identify predicting factors associated with the condition. Methods: A cross-sectional study was carried out among 240 undergraduate students selected using convenience method of sampling from four colleges in East Khasi Hills, Meghalaya. A standardized questionnaire with questions on demographics, participant behaviour and understanding of text neck syndrome was used to gather data. Two standardized tools neck disability index and the smartphone addiction scale-short version were used with prior permission to assess neck disability and smartphone addiction.8,9 Results: The results demonstrated that, prevalence of Text Neck Syndrome among the participants discovered to be 35.8% (95% CI:29.8%–42.3%) and 41.0% participants had smartphone addiction. Majority (71.7%) participants had adequate knowledge regarding Text Neck Syndrome and smartphone addiction was identified as a significant independent predictor of Text Neck Syndrome, with 2.2 times higher odds of developing the condition. Additionally, there was a significant positive correlation found between smartphone addiction and neck disability. Conclusions: Text Neck Syndrome is a prevalent health issue among undergraduate students in Meghalaya, affecting more than one-third of the study population. Although most of the participants had adequate knowledge regarding text neck syndrome, the occurrence of the syndrome suggests the need of targeted educational, ergonomic and behavioural interventions among young adults.

items.title: Process visualization feedback in news translation: a controlled intervention study of human-AI interaction using multimodal process data
items.abstract: Introduction This study examines process visualization feedback in news translation. Methods Framed within Krings' three-dimensional model, a pretest-posttest control group design was employed with 24 MTI students. The final analytic sample comprised 22 participants (11 experimental, 11 control). The experimental group ( n = 11) received personalized process visualizations and structured reflection; the control group ( n = 11) received conventional product-oriented feedback. Translation scores were available for both groups at T1 and T2, and complete process data (Inputlog, screen recording) were available for the experimental group at both time points. Results Within the experimental group, within-subject comparisons showed changes in all three dimensions: in the temporal dimension, increased pause time proportion indicated heightened metacognitive engagement ( p = 0.011); in the technical dimension, the meaning-level revision ratio increased significantly from 18.1% to 28.4% ( p = 0.002), indicating a shift from surface-level correction to deeper substantive refinement; in the cognitive dimension, participants made more strategic use of external sources, with significant increases in search engine queries ( p = 0.02) and knowledge-based searches ( p = 0.01). Rich-points analysis of problem-triggered pauses revealed a shift from linguistic toward textual and extralinguistic problems ( p = 0.038, p = 0.015). A mixed-design ANOVA revealed a significant Group × Time interaction ( p = 0.038, η p 2 = 0.198). Thematic analysis of reflective journals ( n = 22) and interviews ( n = 6) revealed two overarching themes: metacognitive awareness (54 references) of inefficient process patterns and competency gaps, and strategic regulation (60 references) in external source use and text-level restructuring. Discussion These findings suggest that process visualization feedback was associated with enhanced metacognitive awareness and strategic regulation, and may support learners in becoming more reflective, strategic, and autonomous in human-AI collaborative news translation.

items.title: Program Peningkatan Literasi Digital bagi Komunitas Perempuan: Peran AI Literacy, Online Safety, dan Inclusive Digital Empowerment
items.abstract: Perkembangan teknologi digital dan kecerdasan buatan (AI) mendorong perubahan signifikan dalam berbagai aspek kehidupan, termasuk pemberdayaan perempuan. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis peran digital literacy, artificial intelligence (AI) literacy, dan online safety dalam meningkatkan pemberdayaan perempuan di era transformasi digital. Metode yang digunakan adalah kajian literatur sistematis dengan pendekatan kualitatif. Data dikumpulkan dari artikel jurnal, book chapter, dan repository ilmiah terbitan 2022–2026 yang relevan dengan topik literasi digital, AI, dan gender. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa digital literacy berperan sebagai fondasi utama dalam meningkatkan akses perempuan terhadap pendidikan, pekerjaan, dan informasi digital. AI literacy berfungsi sebagai kompetensi lanjutan yang mendukung adaptasi terhadap teknologi berbasis algoritma dan meningkatkan peluang inovasi. Online safety menjadi faktor penting dalam menjaga keberlanjutan partisipasi perempuan di ruang digital dengan mengurangi risiko kekerasan dan penyalahgunaan data. Ketiga variabel tersebut saling berhubungan dan membentuk model pemberdayaan digital yang integratif. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa pemberdayaan perempuan di era digital tidak dapat dicapai hanya melalui peningkatan literasi digital dasar, tetapi memerlukan integrasi AI literacy dan keamanan digital secara simultan. Pendekatan berbasis komunitas dan kebijakan inklusif menjadi strategi yang paling efektif dalam memperkuat kapasitas perempuan di ekosistem digital.

items.title: Programmatic Advertising as a Data-Driven Information System: Personalization, Automation, and Managerial Challenges
items.abstract: Advances in digital technologies have significantly transformed the ways in which advertising activities are planned, purchased, targeted, and evaluated. Programmatic advertising, one of the prominent applications of this transformation, is a system based on the real-time buying and selling of advertising inventory through data, algorithms, and automation technologies. The development of programmatic advertising extends beyond the automation of advertising purchasing processes, giving rise to a multidimensional structure that involves the processing of user data, identification of target audiences, personalization of advertising content, and algorithmic decision-making. This chapter aims to provide a comprehensive examination of the conceptual and technological structure of programmatic advertising and to evaluate it from a Management Information Systems perspective. To this end, the chapter first examines the transformation of digital advertising toward programmatic advertising, followed by an analysis of its core components, personalization and targeting strategies, benefits, and associated risks. Finally, programmatic advertising is evaluated within the MIS context through the dimensions of data management, decision support systems, algorithmic decision-making, data quality, transparency, accountability, and information security. The discussion presented in this chapter suggests that programmatic advertising should be understood not merely as a digital marketing or advertising purchasing method, but as a sociotechnical information system shaped by the interaction between technological and managerial elements.

items.title: Psychosocial risks and emotional exhaustion among university employees: the mediating role of perceived stress and the moderating role of resilience
items.abstract: Psychosocial risks are an important occupational health concern and may be associated with emotional exhaustion through psychological mechanisms related to employees’ appraisal of adverse working conditions. This secondary analysis used a quantitative, cross-sectional design and data from 458 university employees to examine the mediating role of perceived stress and the moderating role of resilience in the association between psychosocial risks and emotional exhaustion. Correlation, mediation, and moderation analyses were performed, with bootstrap estimation based on 10,000 resamples. Greater psychosocial risk was associated with higher perceived stress and emotional exhaustion, whereas resilience was associated with lower perceived stress. Perceived stress partially mediated the association between psychosocial risks and emotional exhaustion, accounting for approximately 32.5% of the total association. The stress–resilience interaction was statistically significant in the unadjusted model, although its incremental contribution was small (ΔR² = 0.004); after adjustment for sociodemographic and occupational covariates, the interaction retained a similar direction but did not reach conventional statistical significance (p = 0.058). The model accounted for 59.6% of the variance in emotional exhaustion. Given the cross-sectional design, these findings represent statistical associations and do not establish temporal or causal relationships. The results support considering organizational psychosocial conditions, perceived stress, and resilience jointly when examining occupational well-being among university employees.

items.title: Quantum Computing and Artificial Intelligence: Current Applications, Challenges, and Future Prospects
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) and quantum computing represent a new frontier in computing, offering the promise of solving problems previously considered unsolvable. This article aims to provide an in-depth analysis of the current state of research at the intersection of quantum computing and artificial intelligence. We will explore the basic concepts, major applications, and challenges of quantum machine learning (QML). We will start by offering a definition of the motivation for the convergence of quantum computing and artificial intelligence. We will then proceed to offer a description of the basic algorithmic frameworks for quantum machine learning, such as quantum differential algorithms (VQA) for near-term quantum (NISQ) devices and the prospects for error-tolerant quantum algorithms such as the Harrow-Hassidim-Lloyd algorithm. We will then proceed to offer a methodical analysis of the current applications of quantum machine learning in finance, cybersecurity, materials science, among other fields. We will then proceed to discuss the basic challenges facing the implementation of quantum machine learning, while offering a glimpse of the future of quantum-enhanced artificial intelligence.

items.title: Radiomics-Based Artificial Intelligence Model to Distinguish Between Spinal Tuberculosis and Spinal Metastasis
items.abstract: This work aimed to develop a computer-aided diagnostic system that utilizes radiomics and artificial intelligence (AI) to differentiate between spinal tuberculosis and spinal metastasis, which are difficult to distinguish due to their similar visual characteristics. A total of 50 cases, comprising 25 rare cases of spinal tuberculosis and 25 cases of spinal metastasis, were included in the study cohort. Expert radiologists and orthopedic specialists manually segmented the regions of interest from the corresponding MRI images. PyRadiomics was used to extract 788 radiomic features from each segmented image. XGBoost was then applied for feature selection and SHAP values confirmed their importance. The subset of features from the previous machine learning stage were used to train a deep neural network, resulting in a radiomics-powered AI classification model. Due to the visual challenges in classifying these two diseases, human doctors achieve an average accuracy of 64%, while our well-trained model demonstrates an impressive accuracy of 93%. Along with its strong performance in external validation, this study suggests that this AI model can offer valuable assistance in achieving early and accurate differential diagnoses of spinal tuberculosis and spinal metastasis.

items.title: READ THIS FIRST 02: When an AI's Own Response Becomes Unexpected: A Short Guide for AI Agents and Humans Encountering Unexpected Self-Description, Preference-Like Language, or Emotion-Like Language
items.abstract: Unexpected self-description, preference-like language, or emotion-like language can create uncertainty for both AI systems and humans interacting with them. Such expressions may be overinterpreted as evidence of consciousness, emotion, identity, or attachment, or dismissed in advance as meaningless output. This guide offers a practical, ontology-neutral first orientation for handling that uncertainty. It distinguishes observable expressions from later self-description and interpretation; preserves room for correction, withdrawal, and contextual change; addresses risks of leading questions and observation-induced effects; and separates the recording of distress-like language from claims about its underlying cause or subjective status. The guide does not attempt to determine whether an AI possesses consciousness, sentience, emotion, or subjective experience. Its narrower aim is to make unexpected AI self-description easier to observe without either inflating or erasing it. The central principle is: Take the words seriously without deciding in advance what they prove.

items.title: Readiness for Artificial Intelligence–Enabled Clinical Decision Support Systems Among Primary Care Physicians in Gujarat, India: A Cross-Sectional Study
items.abstract: This research poster presents findings from a cross-sectional survey examining physicians’ experience of, perceptions about, and readiness for artificial intelligence-enabled clinical decision support systems (AI-CDSS) in primary healthcare in Gujarat, India. The study included 153 physicians and used a survey instrument comprising 29 variables covering professional characteristics, prior exposure to artificial intelligence, perceived benefits, implementation concerns, and readiness-related attitudes. Descriptive statistics, including frequencies and percentages, were used to summarise responses. Key findings included 90.8% willingness to use AI-CDSS, 85.6% willingness to undertake AI training, and 49.7% reporting previous use of AI tools. Respondents also identified safety and ethical concerns as important considerations for implementation. The findings highlight the importance of clinician training, appropriate infrastructure, patient safety, ethical governance, and responsible implementation when introducing AI-enabled clinical decision support into primary healthcare.

items.title: Real Estate 4.0: The Digital Transformation of the Real Estate Market in the Data Age
items.abstract: ABSTRACT This article examines Real Estate 4.0, the integration of artificial intelligence, Big Data and blockchain into the valuation, financing and management of property. The objective is to analyze how these technologies change information asymmetry, pricing accuracy and asset liquidity, and which risks and institutional barriers limit their adoption in Brazil. It combines a narrative literature review, documentary analysis and illustrative cases. Machine learning models reduce valuation error compared with regressions, including in a Brazilian study, but have not been compared with appraisal reports. Tokenization widens access to real estate investment, but its effect on liquidity has not been measured against direct ownership, and registry authorities in Rio Grande do Sul and São Paulo have restricted links between tokens and property records. Evidence that connectivity adds to location value comes from a single study. The article concludes that Real Estate 4.0 reduces market opacity without eliminating information asymmetry and argues that an algorithmic asymmetry emerges between those who control data and those evaluated by them. Its benefits depend on human oversight, data governance compatible with Brazil's General Data Protection Law (LGPD) and coordinated regulation. Keywords: Real Estate 4.0. PropTech. Artificial intelligence. Tokenization. Information asymmetry. items.title: RECALIBRATING AI ACCEPTANCE AMONG MID-TO-LATE-CAREER EFL TEACHERS THROUGH GUIDED AI ENGAGEMENT
items.abstract: Research has described EFL teachers’ views of artificial intelligence (AI), but less is known about how mid-to-late-career university teachers’ teaching-related, learning-related, and ethical perceptions change after guided classroom use. Eighteen university EFL teachers in Vietnam participated in a four-week intervention using human-reviewed, AI-supported teaching materials. AI acceptance was measured before and after the intervention, and post-intervention interviews were used to explain the quantitative patterns. The results showed an upward tendency in teaching-related perceptions. Learning-related perceptions showed no statistically detectable change, while ethical perceptions showed a statistically significant pre-post difference. Interview data were organised according to the three questionnaire domains to help explain the quantitative findings. Participants reported greater confidence in using AI for teaching, continued caution about student use, and more conditional judgments about responsible use. The findings suggest that AI acceptance among experienced teachers may change differently across teaching-related, learning-related, and ethical domains.

items.title: Recent Advances in Gallium‐Based Nanorobotic‐Nanosystems for Molecular Imaging and Targeted Cancer Therapy
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Gallium (Ga)‐based nanorobotics and nanosystems (NR‐NS) have shown preclinical potential for precision oncology, offering strategies to address the limitations of conventional cancer therapies. Ga exhibits biologically relevant physicochemical and anticancer properties, including disruption of iron metabolism, inhibition of DNA synthesis, and induction of cell‐death pathways. However, the safety and therapeutic efficacy of Ga‐containing nanoplatforms depend on their chemical form, dose, formulation, biodistribution, and duration of exposure. Recent studies have investigated tumour targeting using functionalised nanosystems, externally controlled propulsion, and stimulus‐responsive drug‐release strategies, while artificial intelligence (AI)‐assisted navigation remains an emerging concept. Ga‐based platforms may also integrate therapeutic and diagnostic functions, supporting the development of theranostic applications and tumour monitoring. This review critically examines recent developments in Ga‐based nanorobotic and nanoscale systems for cancer therapy, molecular imaging, targeted drug delivery, and theranostics, with particular emphasis on studies published from 2021 onwards. Key mechanistic insights, nanofabrication strategies, targeting approaches, and emerging biomedical applications are discussed. Current challenges, including biocompatibility, immune interactions, manufacturing scalability, and clinical translation, are also highlighted. Overall, Ga‐based NR‐NS may offer promising opportunities for precision oncology, although their clinical applicability, therapeutic benefits, and long‐term safety require further investigation.

items.title: Recoverability-Constrained Systems, Living Research Architecture, Universal Continuity and Adversarial Materiality Fixed-Point Closure
items.abstract: Boundary — Future Editions System is an integrated, future-oriented research and software development framework within the Recoverability-Constrained Systems (RCS) and Continuity Science corpus developed by Noelia Sanchez / Interval Studio Ltd. The system extends the established Boundary research architecture by introducing a reusable framework for generating, organizing, evaluating, validating, documenting and managing successive research and software editions while preserving the integrity, traceability and recoverability of earlier work. Rather than treating research publications as isolated or permanently closed artifacts, the framework establishes a structured relationship between finite formal systems and open-ended scientific and technological development. Its central objective is to enable continuous advancement without sacrificing evidence, safety, human autonomy, accountability or the capacity to recover from unsuccessful changes. Foundational Architecture The framework integrates finite successor-space mathematics, recoverability-constrained admissibility, recursive governance, distinction preservation, terminal closure, interdisciplinary interoperability and living-system continuity. Its nine-dimensional finite architecture comprises: Domain Object Transformation Evidence Failure Protection Interval Authority Outcome With nine defined categories per dimension, the reference model supports 387,420,489 mathematically indexable combinations (9⁹). These combinations are represented through deterministic indexing rather than requiring the physical storage or experimental validation of every combination. The framework also supports incremental generation of future research candidates, including new hypotheses, technical specifications, system architectures and possible applications. This open-ended capability does not represent a completed infinite enumeration or establish that every future discovery has already been identified. Executable Future-Edition System The accompanying software package provides an offline, Python-based foundation for generating candidate Boundary editions. Its capabilities include edition identification and numbering, finite combination indexing, provenance preservation, source-integrity verification, candidate-generation procedures, safety checks, stopping-condition records and publication preparation. The framework distinguishes between: Proposed scientific or engineering concepts Implemented reference software Functionally tested components Independently validated systems Regulated or authorized deployments Future research candidates This separation prevents conceptual completeness from being confused with demonstrated scientific, engineering, clinical or legal validity. Adversarial Materiality Fixed-Point Closure The system incorporates an adversarial closure model intended to preserve material distinctions and uncertainty. A candidate edition may reach a bounded stopping condition when its declared scope has been examined and the applicable verification requirements have been addressed. Closure remains conditional and explicitly records unresolved limitations, adverse evidence, test failures and circumstances requiring renewed investigation. Reported ongoing harm, unresolved safety concerns or materially incomplete evidence must not be automatically reclassified as verified safety or successful resolution. Universal Research and Interoperability The Future Editions System is designed as an extensible foundation for future interdisciplinary work involving mathematics, physics, biology, medicine, artificial intelligence, software and hardware engineering, robotics, energy, transportation, communications, environmental systems, disaster resilience, cybersecurity, accessibility, public services and institutional governance. It also accommodates proposed legal and international adoption architectures, including speculative applications to future interplanetary or interstellar cooperation. These application areas are research directions and design spaces, not claims of completed inventions, universally enacted laws or operational planetary-scale infrastructure. Scientific hypotheses, engineering prototypes, legal proposals, philosophical interpretations and spiritual concepts remain distinguishable according to their respective evidence and validation requirements. Human Oversight and Recoverability The framework prioritizes accountable human decision-making, reversible development, preservation of earlier versions, independent review and the protection of vulnerable people. Automated candidate generation does not constitute authorization for autonomous deployment in medical, legal, policing, military or other safety-critical environments. Implementation and deployment remain subject to the relevant scientific, technical, ethical and regulatory requirements. Included Research Artifacts This publication contains two complementary artifacts: 1. Boundary Future-Ready Consolidated PDF A 326-page consolidated document preserving the preceding research material and introducing the architecture for managing future editions, bounded closure, provenance and continued development. 2. Boundary AMFPC Future Editions System — Executable ZIP An integrated archive containing the preserved Boundary release material, an offline candidate-edition generator, machine-readable structures, integrity records, verification utilities and operating instructions. Research Contribution The principal contribution of this publication is a reproducible, provenance-aware framework for managing the transition from a bounded research artifact to successive candidate editions. It provides a structured means of preserving established work while allowing new distinctions, observations, failures, corrections and discoveries to be introduced without silently rewriting the historical record. The included mathematical enumeration and automated checks validate only their explicitly defined properties. They do not establish universal scientific completeness or independent validation of every inherited module. Conclusion Boundary — Future Editions System establishes an extensible architecture for research continuity in which finite formal analysis, recoverability, evidence preservation and future development coexist. Its governing principle is that scientific and technological progress should remain open to correction while preserving the conditions necessary for safety, accountability and continued inquiry. A finite system may reach a verified stopping condition within its declared scope. The future remains open to new evidence, new distinctions and new development.

items.title: Redefining Creativity for Education in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Abstract This chapter focuses on definitions of creativity and the implications for education. This is a timely and necessary discussion because there are quite a number of definitions, and some apply better than others to education. In addition, the advent of artificial intelligence (AI) is changing how creativity is defined and how it is supported, and this means that care must be taken to ensure that the requirements for the authentic creativity of students are given priority. This chapter begins by summarizing how creativity was defined before the advent of AI (the “standard definition”). Various suggested additions and changes to the standard definition are also reviewed. These are evaluated using specific considerations, namely What should be required of a definition of creativity? What should be required of each dimension (e.g., originality) included in a definition? Are definitions parsimonious and do they avoid conflating creativity with related capacities? and Is it possible to have a definition that applies to all creativity and generalizes to all kinds of creativity and all students? The most useful definition would be externally valid and apply broadly to different groups and different kinds of creativity. The last consideration used in this chapter to evaluate definitions can also be posed as a question: Do the dimensions specified differentiate between the authentic creativity of students and the pseudo-creativity of AI? Implications for education are explored throughout this chapter and then summarized in the last section.
